This file gives Claude (and other AI assistants) the context needed to work effectively in this repository.

Package Overview

plot2 is a high-level R wrapper around ggplot2 designed to minimise typing while producing complex, publication-ready plots. The central idea: one call to plot2() replaces many separate ggplot2 + dplyr/tidyr steps, including automatic plot-type selection, in-line data transformations, axis handling, and custom theming.

  • CRAN/GitHub: https://github.com/msberends/plot2
  • Docs site: https://msberends.github.io/plot2
  • License: GPL-2
  • Requires R ≥ 4.1.0, ggplot2 ≥ 4.0.0

Coding Style

Formatting

  • Indentation: 2 spaces (set in plot2.Rproj; no tabs).
  • Line length: keep readable; wrap long parameter lists with one argument per line.
  • Braces: opening brace on the same line as the control structure or function header.

Naming

Kind Convention Example
Exported functions snake_case plot2(), get_colour(), theme_minimal2()
Internal helpers snake_case (no prefix) like(), font_black(), group_sizes()
S3 methods function.class plot2.data.frame, format2.Date
Package environment plot2_env plot2_env$reg_cols
Internal NSE columns _var_x, _var_y, … prefixed with _ to avoid clashes
Options plot2.<name> plot2.colour, plot2.font

File Headers

Every .R source file starts with the same 73-character-wide box comment block:

# ===================================================================== #
#  An R package for Fast 'ggplot2' Plotting:                            #
#  https://github.com/msberends/plot2                                   #
#                                                                       #
#  This R package is free software; you can freely use and distribute   #
#  it for both personal and commercial purposes under the terms of the  #
#  GNU General Public License version 2.0 (GNU GPL-2), as published by  #
#  the Free Software Foundation.                                        #
#                                                                       #
#  We created this package for both routine data analysis and academic  #
#  research and it was publicly released in the hope that it will be    #
#  useful, but it comes WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY OR LIABILITY.              #
# ===================================================================== #

New files must include this header verbatim at the top.

Documentation (roxygen2)

  • Markdown is enabled (Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE) in DESCRIPTION).
  • Use [function()], [pkg::function()], and [topic] links freely.
  • Parameter lists for multi-possibility arguments use a bullet list under @param.
  • Group related functions with @rdname.
  • Every exported function must have a @examples block.
  • Internal helpers use @keywords internal (no @export).
  • Never edit man/ or NAMESPACE by hand – always regenerate with devtools::document().
  • Roxygen blocks must end with @examples.
#' Short Title
#'
#' @description Full description. The [plot2()] function …
#'
#' @param .data Data to plot.
#' @param x One of:
#' - A single variable, e.g. `x = column1`
#' - A function, e.g. `x = format(date, "%Y")`
#'
#' @return A [`ggplot`][ggplot2::ggplot()] object.
#' @export
#' @examples
#' iris |> plot2(Species)

Error / Warning Handling

  • Always use call. = FALSE:

    stop("message", call. = FALSE)
warning("message", call. = FALSE)

  • Use the package’s own wrappers for user-facing messages:

    plot2_message("informational text")   # coloured blue via crayon
plot2_warning("warning text")         # coloured yellow

NSE (Non-Standard Evaluation)

  • Internal temporary columns are prefixed with _ (e.g., _var_x, _var_category).
  • All such names are declared in globalVariables() inside R/utils.R to suppress R CMD check notes. Add new NSE names there when needed.

Custom Operators (defined in R/utils.R)

Operator Purpose
%like% Case-insensitive regex match (grepl wrapper)
%unlike% Negated %like%
%>% Re-exported pipe from dplyr
%+replace% ggplot2 theme replacement (imported)

Testing

  • Framework: testthat edition 3 (Config/testthat/edition: 3 in DESCRIPTION); vdiffr and withr in Suggests.
  • Infrastructure (see #156):
    • helper-plot2.R: accessors (geoms(), layer_df(), label_text(), axis_breaks(), axis_labels(), scale_values(), theme_el(), facet_info(), col_hex(), …), plot2_diagnostics(), and expectations (expect_plot2(), expect_geoms(), expect_labels(), expect_axis_breaks(), expect_scale_values(), expect_facets(), expect_plot2_message(), expect_clean_state(), expect_plot2_snapshot()). Every custom expectation reports exactly one result.
    • helper-fixtures.R: small deterministic fixtures fx_*; add shared data there, not inline.
    • setup.R: deterministic environment (UTC, C locale, plot2 options reset).
    • test-helpers.R: self-tests of the helpers; extend it whenever a helper is added or changed.
  • Test files: per-topic files only; the smoke tests of the former test_plot2.R are in test-legacy-*.R (skipped on CRAN). Topic prefixes: test-plot2_exec-E<nn>-<topic>.R (stages of plot2_exec()), test-modules-M<nn>-<topic>.R (methods and modules), test-api-A<nn> (documented behaviour), test-themes-T<nn> (cross-cutting themes), test-shiny-S<nn> (Shiny server, driven with the shiny_*() helpers) and test-validate-<nn> (one file per validate.R function). Every test_that() description starts with its case ID (e.g. "E05.03 ..."); in test-regression-*.R the ID is the GitHub issue number (e.g. "#13 ...").
  • Tests for open GitHub issues describe the desired behaviour and start with skip_open_issue("#123"). When fixing the issue, remove that line and the test must pass. Known soft deprecations caused by plot2 are silenced per test with local_known_deprecation("#123"), never globally.
  • Test content, not only class: prefer expect_geoms(), expect_labels() etc. over expect_s3_class(p, "gg"). expect_plot2() renders the plot and fails on R warnings.
  • CRAN core (#50): on CRAN the suite runs without the legacy smoke tests (test-legacy-*.R), the Shiny server tests (shiny_app() skips), the help page, vignette and README tests, visual snapshots and timing guards; about 2 minutes in total. Guard every use of a suggested package with skip_if_not_installed().
  • The full suite takes several minutes: run it detached and read the log.

Rscript -e "devtools::test()"

Key Patterns

S3 Dispatch

plot2() uses S3 dispatch to handle different input classes. The generic is in R/plot2.R; methods are in R/plot2-methods.R:

plot2.default      – vectors, and objects that broom::augment() or ggplot2::fortify() turn into a data frame (e.g. lm, table)
plot2.data.frame   – the primary method (most logic lives here)
plot2.matrix       – correlation matrices → heatmap
plot2.sf           – simple features / geographic data
plot2.freq         – cleaner::freq() tables
plot2.formula      – formula interface

Colour S3 Class

get_colour.R defines a colour vctrs-compatible S3 class with methods for as.character, print, c, rep, rev, unique, and vec_cast. Users register project colours with register_colour() / unregister_colour(); they are stored in plot2_env$reg_cols.

Parameter Grouping Convention

plot2() parameter names follow a consistent dot-namespacing pattern:

Prefix Controls
x. x-axis settings (x.title, x.sort, x.max_items, …)
y. y-axis settings (y.title, y.transform, y.limits, …)
facet. facet settings (facet.nrow, facet.position, …)
datalabels. data-label settings (datalabels.size, datalabels.colour, …)
smooth. smoothing settings
y_secondary., title., subtitle., legend. settings of these elements

Naming rule (see API Decisions below): <argument>.<setting> only where the part before the dot is itself a plot2() argument, with the setting in snake case (x.label_angle, facet.repeat_labels_x); everything else is plain snake case (colour_fill, sankey_node_width, jitter_seed). Exceptions: base-R names na.rm, na.replace, decimal.mark, big.mark; and legend.value in the add_*() functions. Automatic defaults are NULL in the usage (#106); explicit values mean what they say. Options are prefixed plot2. (e.g. plot2.decimal.mark).

Single argument definition (#47): the arguments are defined once, in the generic plot2() in R/plot2.R. The methods and plot2_exec() get their formals in R/zzz.R (plot2_method_formals()), and forward everything with eval(plot2_exec_call()). A new argument is added only to the generic (plus its @param), and used in plot2_exec().

validate_*() Functions

All argument validation happens in dedicated validate_*() functions in R/validate.R (e.g., validate_type(), validate_legend.position()). Keep validation out of the main function body.

Adding New Plot Types

  1. Add type aliases/detection in R/validate.R inside validate_type().
  2. Implement the geom layer in R/plot2.R (or a dedicated file like R/back2back_plot.R for complex types).
  3. Register any new NSE column names in globalVariables() in R/utils.R.
  4. Add @importFrom tags and re-run devtools::document().
  5. Write tests in a per-topic file in tests/testthat/ using the helpers in helper-plot2.R.
  6. Document the new type in the @param type block in R/plot2.R and update vignettes/supported_types.Rmd.

  • Current version: see DESCRIPTION.

Issues and History

  • Work is tracked in GitHub issues (https://github.com/msberends/plot2/issues). Refer to them in code, comments and tests as #123.
  • The review and overhaul of 2026-11 (milestone v2.0.0, issues #13 to #160) was done in a folder review_and_overhaul/ that has since been removed; its findings and ideas are now closed issues, and the full working material (review sheets, reproductions, journal) is in the git history before its removal.

API Decisions

The maintainer’s decisions on argument names and defaults, made before the first CRAN release (from proposal #159). The package is not on CRAN, is beta and has no known users, so breaking changes are made directly, without aliases or deprecation, until the first CRAN release. API changes need the maintainer’s consent per item, not per group.

Design principle

plot2 exists to streamline ggplot2, whose API requires knowledge of hundreds of arguments across tens of functions. User-facing concepts (type, category) come first; ggplot2 concepts (geoms, aesthetics) stay in the background. Follow ggplot2’s names where that is not unclear or complex, and depart from them where it helps users.

Naming rule

<argument>.<setting> with the setting in snake case, only where the part before the dot is itself a plot2() argument (x, y, category, facet, y_secondary, title, subtitle, datalabels, smooth, legend); everything else is plain snake case. Exceptions: base-R names na.rm, na.replace, decimal.mark, big.mark; and legend.value in add_line(), add_point(), add_col() and add_smooth().

Decided items

Item Decision
Automatic defaults NULL in the usage, documented as “determined automatically”; explicit values mean what they say (#106).
colour_opacity, get_colour(opacity = ) Renamed to colour_transparency and transparency, same meaning (0 = solid, 1 = transparent).
x.lbl_angle, x.lbl_align, x.lbl_italic Renamed to x.label_angle, x.label_align, x.label_italic.
facet.repeat_lbls_x, facet.repeat_lbls_y Renamed to facet.repeat_labels_x, facet.repeat_labels_y.
sankey.node_width, sankey.node_whitespace, sankey.alpha, sankey.remove_axes Renamed to sankey_node_width, sankey_node_whitespace, sankey_alpha, sankey_remove_axes (there is no sankey argument).
facet.fill Renamed to facet.colour_fill.
Options dec_mark, big_mark Renamed to plot2.decimal.mark, plot2.big.mark; the functions dec_mark() and big_mark() keep their names and read these options.
x.mic, x.lbl_taxonomy Removed from plot2(); replaced by separate helpers (e.g. label_taxonomy()).
legend New argument: NULL (automatic), TRUE forces, FALSE hides. The legend is only the plot element explaining category; the legend.* settings keep their names.
legend.position Keeps "none" as an alternative way to hide; NULL means automatic.
legend.title, category.title Both kept as one setting; giving both stops with an error.
stacked, stacked_fill Both kept; stacked = "fill" equals stacked_fill = TRUE; on conflict stacked_fill = TRUE wins.
Kept as they are jitter_seed, violin_scale, category.type, the prefix y_secondary.

Renamed and removed arguments give a clear error (plot2_old_args in R/zzz.R).
